root.name: Danish Gambit Accepted: Schlechter Defense
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. d4 exd4 3. c3 dxc3 4. Bc4 cxb2 5. Bxb2 d5

overview: In the Danish Gambit Accepted Black plays 5...d5, returning a pawn to counter the bishops. White plays 6.Bxd5 or 6.exd5, regaining one pawn with a lead in development, and the b2 bishop and c4 bishop aim at the kingside. Black must be careful with the king, but the extra material gives Black a safe edge with accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Regain one pawn with Bxd5 and attack the Black king with the bishops and queen
Use the open diagonals and quick development

black_ideas.idea: Neutralise the bishops with ...d5 and ...Nf6 and consolidate
Trade queens and keep the extra pawn

typical_structures.structure: Open position with White bishops on b2 and c4
Black pawn majority on the kingside

character.notes: Open, forcing play with White down material for development.

gambit.notes: White is two pawns down at the root; 5...d5 returns one.

soundness.notes: Danish Gambit is unsound against accurate defence.

structure.notes: Central pawns are traded and lines are open.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly choose the Danish.

level.notes: Gambit lines with forcing tactics, though dubious.
